name: High-Girth Partial Cubes Are Tree-Zone and Sparse
statement: Let $G$ be a finite or locally finite partial cube with $g(G)>6$. Every zone graph is a tree. If $\delta(G)\ge3$, then $G$ contains an infinite subtree of degrees two and three with degree-two vertices pairwise at distance at least two; hence $G$ is infinite and has exponential growth. A finite regular such graph is $K_1$, $K_2$, or an even cycle.
comments: The strict girth bound is sharp: middle-levels graphs have girth six.
